correctness.rationale: Conditional on (V,Z), the Xi are iid N(sqrt(1-2V) Z/2,V). Conditional on V, Xi+Xj is centered Gaussian of variance (1-2V)+2V=1 for every distinct i,j. Direct conditional covariances give diagonal 1/4+EV/2 and off-diagonal 1/4-EV/2. A centered normal variance mixture has fourth cumulant 3 Var((1+2V)/4)=3 Var(V)/4, strictly positive if rho is not a point mass. The difference cancels Z and has conditional char fn exp(-V t^2), the Laplace transform uniquely determines the finite mixing law. Independent Fraction arithmetic checked both explicit examples, including cumulants 0 and 3/256. These are exact algebraic calculations, not a finite experiment in place of a general proof.

value.rationale: An explicit infinite exchangeable counterfamily locates a sharp observational weakness immediately adjacent to published Gaussian rigidity: scalar Gaussianity of every pair sum plus the whole covariance matrix cannot force Gaussian process structure. The opposing difference law exactly identifies the hidden variance mixing measure. A continuum of laws and explicit Gaussian/non-Gaussian pair give a meaningful testable distinction rather than a routine normalization check; nonidentifiability in general is not newly claimed.

final_claim: For arbitrary Borel law rho on (0,1/2), the indicated infinite exchangeable conditional-Gaussian sequence has all pair sums N(0,1), covariance determined by E V alone, marginal fourth cumulant 3 Var(V)/4, and pair-difference characteristic transform int exp(-v t^2)rho(dv) identifying rho. Gaussian and non-Gaussian covariance-matched examples exist.
